images.prompt: An extraordinarily detailed cinematic matte painting in the exact finished science-fiction environment art direction of the reference: monumental weathered orbital network infrastructure with richly rendered surfaces, precise mechanical engineering and dramatic naturalistic volumetric lighting. The epic establishing view of the Line, a colossal ring of relay machinery circling a cloud-wrapped world at the edge of space, seen from high above at dawn. The ring is a continuous band of dark relay halls, trusses, cable-hung platforms and stacked containers; its long arc sweeps across the upper frame from the left and curves away into the far distance as a thin line of tiny amber lights. Gigantic relay spires, dark industrial lattice towers wrapped in gantries, conduits and lift shafts, rise from an endless sea of clouds far below to meet and hold up the ring; the nearest spire stands in the right middle ground with small warm windows. Far along the arc, immense circular ring gates face outward toward the stars. The first golden sunlight breaks over the horizon of the cloud sea, lighting the cloud tops and the brass edges of the ring; the upper sky is deep blue-black with stars, a large pale planet and a small moon hang in it. Gothic spire shapes appear only as tiny distant silhouettes. Dense layers of trusses, fine gantries, bundled cables and conduits, riveted dark-brass panels, worn ivory ceramic machinery and tiny service lights establish convincing colossal scale. Sophisticated chiaroscuro, deep desaturated midnight-blue shadows, small warm amber highlights and restrained teal signal light, intricate sharp foreground detail gradually lost in immense misty distance. Finished high-end game environment key art with rich oil-painting texture and subtle painterly edge control, never sketchy. images.prompt: An antique engraved plate from an ancient technical manual: a finely etched copperplate illustration printed in dark sepia-brown ink on aged ivory paper, with delicate touches of gilt. Dense fine line hatching and cross-hatching, stippled shading, precise mechanical draughtsmanship, the look of a centuries-old engineering folio. The engraving shows the raising of a colossal relay spire out of a sea of clouds, drawn as ancient network machinery rather than a plain tower: a tall tapering spire of trusses bristling with relay dishes, antenna arrays, stacked insulators, cable conduits and relay node housings, wrapped in scaffolding; an enormous curved segment of the orbital ring, carrying bundled fibre conduits and rows of relay node pods, hoisted into place by tall lattice cranes; giant cable drums unreeling thick fibre bundles; tiny hooded figures in sealed work suits with round helmet visors on the scaffolds splicing cable. Gilt touches pick out the relay nodes and the ring. Billowing engraved clouds below, the finished arc of the ring crossing the engraved sky above, a planet disc near the horizon. The engraving fills the whole widescreen frame. No writing, lettering, captions, numbers or labels anywhere. No oil painting, no colour photography, no 3D rendering, no swords, torches, scrolls or medieval props.
